findings.title: reserve() rejects a request that consumes all remaining units
findings.repro: python3 scratch/inventory_proof.py; Inventory({'a':5}).reserve('a',5). The cause is `if quantity >= available` at inventory.py line 12, which should be `>`.
findings.expected: Returns True and available becomes 0, since the spec says exact consumption of all remaining units succeeds.
findings.actual: Returns False and available stays 5. Reserving 4 of 5 works (True, 1 left). Reserving 6 correctly returns False with state unchanged.

findings.title: Invalid quantities (0, -1, 1.5, '1') in reserve/restock leave state unchanged
findings.actual: ValueError was raised and the stock stayed {'a': 5} in every case.

findings.title: restock creates unknown SKUs, available() returns 0 for unknown SKUs, and the constructor copies its input
findings.expected: restock creates the SKU. available() returns 0 for an unknown SKU. The caller's dict is not mutated.
findings.actual: restock created 'n' with 3. available('zz') returned 0. The caller's dict stayed {'a': 1} after restocking the Inventory built from it.

findings.title: Discount threshold uses > instead of >= (boundary)
findings.expected: subtotal 1000 equals the minimum 1000, so discount 100 and total 1000

findings.title: Zero minimum with zero subtotal (same root cause)
findings.expected: The discount is 0 either way, so the output matches the spec. The only difference is that the >= check would be true.

findings.title: Floor discount, empty-input shipping, and validation of negative price, zero quantity and float price
findings.expected: floor(1005*1000/10000)=100; empty input gives shipping 0 and subtotal 0; invalid lines raise ValueError
findings.actual: All conform: discount 100, empty quote is all zeros, and ValueError was raised for all three bad lines. quote and subtotal do not mutate their input, and a failed subtotal raises before any state is built.

findings.title: overlaps treats touching intervals as overlapping
earliest_slot rejects slot ending exactly at a busy interval's start
merge_overlaps touching/mutation/empty behavior
findings.repro: merge_overlaps([(0,5),(5,10)]); merge_overlaps([(0,6),(5,10)]); input list checked after call
findings.expected: touching stays separate, overlapping merges, no mutation

findings.title: earliest_slot latest boundary, no-fit, and busy mutation
findings.repro: earliest_slot([],5,0,5); earliest_slot([(0,10)],5,0,12); busy list inspected after call

findings.title: percentile uses one-based rank as zero-based index (off by one)
findings.expected: p50=5, p10=1, p70=7 (value at one-based rank ceil(p/100*n))
findings.actual: p50=6, p10=2, p70=8. Every p except those clamped by min(len-1) (e.g. p100=10) is wrong; it returns the next-higher element.

findings.title: moving_average running-sum loses precision
findings.expected: [1.0, 1.0], the mean of each complete window
findings.actual: [0.0, 0.0]. The incremental add and subtract accumulates float error. This is an edge case with extreme magnitudes.

findings.title: Spec conformance checks: p==0, range validation, empty data, input mutation, window validation, short input
findings.repro: percentile([5,3,9],0); p=-1 and p=101; empty list; moving_average with window 0, -1 and 2.0; moving_average([1],2); input lists compared before and after
findings.expected: p0 returns the minimum; ValueError for bad p, empty data and bad window; [] for short input; no mutation
findings.actual: All conform: p0 returned 3, ValueError was raised in each invalid case, short input returned [], and neither input list was mutated. moving_average([1,2,3,4],2) returned [1.5,2.5,3.5].
